Developers

Send W3 results to PRMS directly from your own platform, in a standard format, individually or in bulk, instead of reporting them by hand.

How to integrate

Five steps from nothing to results landing in PRMS.

1 Request your test API key Ask for a key for the test environment first. Your key identifies your platform on every call.
2 Read the field documentation Check which fields your result type needs and which values PRMS matches against the CLARISA catalogues.
3 Send a result to the test environment Post one result to single result ingest and confirm the response. Add your own external_reference so you can match the response to your record.
4 Register a webhook Point PRMS at an HTTPS endpoint of yours to find out when a Science Program approves or rejects a result. Optional, but decisions taken before you register are not sent again.
5 Request your production key and switch Same payload, different key and different URLs. Never reuse the test key in production.
Get an API key

Every call needs a CLARISA API key in the x-api-key header. There is no anonymous access. Keys are issued by the PRMS team, one per platform and per environment: never reuse a key across tools or between test and production, because the key is what identifies your platform to PRMS.

Tell us which platform it is for and which environment you need.
Environments

Test your integration against the test environment before you send anything to production.

Test
API reference (Swagger) https://v2f4lv8av4.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/docs/
Single result ingest https://v2f4lv8av4.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/ingest
Bulk ingest https://0w16ghmybe.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/ingest
Production
API reference (Swagger) https://v6a9z2e4y5.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/docs
Single result ingest https://v6a9z2e4y5.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/ingest
Bulk ingest https://bla4fsvgni.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/ingest
Use single result ingest for one to ten results, and bulk ingest for more.
Field documentation

The full field reference covers the seven result types, the minimum data standards for each, the CLARISA catalogues the values are matched against, and the breaking changes log.

Result decision webhooks

Register an HTTPS callback with your API key and PRMS will notify you when a Science Program approves or rejects one of your results, with the reviewer's justification. Register it before your results go under review: decisions taken with no destination registered are not sent again.

What you still do in PRMS

Two things the API cannot carry:

Confidential evidence. The API accepts public links only. Evidence that cannot be public is uploaded in the reporting tool.
Fields beyond the minimum data standards. Send keep_editing as true and the result arrives as Editing, so the reporting user completes it and submits it from PRMS.

Questions about the API? Contact the PRMS technical team.

Notifications

AI Assistant for result Titles and Descriptions: PRMS includes an AI assistant that generates suggested titles and descriptions for results based on the information entered by users. During the 2025 reporting cycle, its use contributed to a reduction in QA comments on result titles and descriptions, from 28% to 16%. Based on this positive experience and user feedback, we encourage Programs/Accelerators to use the AI assistant to improve the quality and consistency of reported results. To use the assistant, click AI Review once it becomes available. The button is automatically enabled after the required data fields that trigger the AI assistant have been completed. All AI-generated text should be carefully reviewed, validated, and, where necessary, refined before submission.

AI-assisted Notification for Impact Area Scores: PRMS includes an AI assistant that reviews the result's metadata (and supporting evidence for scores of 2), it assesses whether the information provided is consistent with and adequately supports the selected score, and flags potential mismatches. The assistant does not select or recommend a score; responsibility for assigning the score remains with the user. To use the assistant, click AI Review once it becomes available. Any AI-generated notifications should be carefully reviewed and used to validate, and, where necessary, revise the selected Impact Area score and its supporting evidence before submission.

Score the relevance of this result for each of the five Impact Areas.

0 — Not targeted: screened against the Impact Area but does not directly contribute to any of its aspects.

1 — Significant: contributes directly to one or more aspects, but that is not the principal objective of the result.

2 — Principal: contributing to the Impact Area is the principal objective. The activity would not have been undertaken without it.

Every result needs at least one score of 1 or 2. No more than two Impact Areas can be scored 2. Score on relevance to the Impact Area as defined in the CGIAR 2030 Research and Innovation Strategy, not on donor interest.
